fullDescription:
Hong Island in the late afternoon, when the day boats have left and the lagoon is quiet.

Koh Hong's centrepiece is its lagoon, a near-enclosed pool of shallow green water ringed by limestone walls and reached through a gap boats can only enter at certain tides. By late afternoon the mooring lines that crowd it at midday are gone. The sheltered bays around the island are where the snorkelling happens; the water here stays calmer than the open crossings because the island group blocks the swell.

Ko Pak Bia is the other stop, and it is barely an island at all. It is a sandbar with a fringe of trees whose shape changes with every tide, so the strip you walk on is not the one in the photograph you saw. That is the appeal rather than a disappointment.

The barbecue is cooked and served as the sun goes down. Limestone holds colour for a long time after sunset, so the good light lasts well past the point you would expect it to end.

The trip closes with a plankton swim. Bioluminescent dinoflagellates flash when the water around them moves, so the light appears around your hands and feet rather than across the surface. It is genuinely variable: dark nights near a new moon show it best, a full moon washes it out, and choppy water scatters it. Worth asking about the moon phase before fixing a date.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers hotel pickup and drop-off, the boat with crew and guide, snorkelling equipment, barbecue dinner, drinking water, soft drinks and fruit, life jackets and insurance.

Six to seven hours. National park fees are collected at the pier unless confirmed otherwise, so carry cash. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Hong Island lagoon after the day boats have gone
Snorkelling in the island's sheltered bays
Ko Pak Bia sandbar, reshaped by every tide
Barbecue dinner cooked as the sun sets
Plankton swim, best on dark nights near a new moon

fullDescription:
A seat at the Muay Thai stadium on Ko Lanta, which is a very different evening from the big-city arenas.

Muay Thai is Thailand's national sport and an eight-limb striking art: fists, elbows, knees and shins all count, which is what separates it from boxing and from kickboxing. A card runs several bouts through the evening, starting with the youngest and least experienced fighters and building to the main events, so arriving early means watching the sport at its rawest and arriving late means watching it at its most skilled.

Every fight opens with the Wai Khru Ram Muay, a slow ritual dance in which the fighter pays respect to teacher and family and seals the ring. It is not a warm-up and it is not for the audience; it predates the sport's commercial form entirely. The live band plays the sarama, an oboe-and-drum rhythm that speeds up as the fight intensifies, which is the detail most first-time spectators remember afterwards.

The island stadium is small. You are close enough to hear the impact of a shin on a forearm, the crowd is a mix of locals betting and travellers watching, and nobody is performing for a tour group. The bigger Bangkok stadiums are more polished; this is more honest.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers one seat ticket. Food, drinks and transport are not included, so plan how you are getting there and back.

Schedules vary by week rather than running nightly, so the date is confirmed with the stadium before your booking is final. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Thailand's national sport in a small island stadium
Wai Khru Ram Muay ritual before every bout
Live sarama band that speeds up with the fight
Undercard first, main events later in the night
Close enough to hear the strikes land

fullDescription:
An hour on the trails behind Krabi, which is the short version for people who want the ride without giving up half a day.

The route runs through rubber and oil-palm plantation on red clay tracks, with limestone outcrops rising out of the fields on either side. It is a different Krabi from the coastline that fills the brochures: working agricultural land, a few kilometres inland, where the terrain is rolling rather than flat.

Condition of the trails follows the season. From November to April the clay is firm and fast. From May onwards the rain turns it properly muddy, which most riders find is the better version even though nobody stays clean.

No licence is required and no previous experience is assumed. There is a briefing and a short practice loop before the guide leads out, and the pace is set by the slowest rider rather than the fastest. An hour is enough to get comfortable on the machine and still feel like you rode something.

Wear clothes and closed shoes you do not mind ruining. Contact lenses and dust do not mix, so glasses are the better choice if you have both.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers the ATV ride, hotel pickup and drop-off, a professional English-speaking guide, seasonal fruit, drinking water, safety equipment and travel insurance.

Ninety minutes including transfers, minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Clay trails through rubber and palm plantation
Firm and fast November to April, muddy after May
No licence or riding experience needed
Briefing and practice loop before heading out
Hotel pickup, safety gear, fruit and water included

fullDescription:
Eleven hours that covers Krabi's inland half in the morning and its islands in the evening, which is the only way to see both in one day.

The morning is spent away from the coast entirely. Krabi's interior is limestone and rainforest, with spring-fed pools and waterfalls that run cool even in April when the coast is at its hottest, and a viewpoint that puts the whole karst landscape in one frame. Almost nobody on a beach holiday goes inland, which is exactly why it is worth the early start.

The afternoon and evening take the boat out to Railay, the sandbank at Thale Waek, Poda, Tup and Mor. Railay is a peninsula cut off from the road network by limestone headlands, so it is reachable only by boat. Thale Waek, the Separated Sea, is a strip of sand that links islands at low tide and disappears at high tide, which is why the schedule follows the tide table rather than the clock.

Snorkelling happens where the water is clear enough to justify it, and sunset is taken from the boat among the islands.

Eleven hours is a genuinely long day and the combination is the point: if you only have one day in Krabi and cannot choose between jungle and islands, this is the trip that refuses to choose.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers hotel pickup and drop-off in Krabi, an English-speaking guide, the boat trip to Railay, the sandbank, Poda, Tup and Mor, and snorkelling mask and equipment.

National park fees are collected at the pier unless confirmed otherwise, so carry cash. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Inland waterfalls and viewpoint in the morning
Spring-fed pools that stay cool through April
Railay, the sandbank, Poda, Tup and Mor by boat
Tide-timed, because the sandbank only appears at low water
One day that covers both halves of Krabi

fullDescription:
Phi Phi and the Krabi four islands in a single day, run on a speed catamaran rather than a speedboat.

The boat matters on this route. A nine-hour day covering both Phi Phi and the local islands means a lot of open water, and a catamaran's twin hulls stay considerably steadier through chop than a monohull speedboat does. If anyone in your group is prone to seasickness, this is the version of the day to book.

Phi Phi Leh holds Maya Bay, which closed entirely from 2018 to 2022 so the reef could recover and reopened under strict conditions: boats moor at the back of the island and visitors walk in, swimming inside the bay is restricted, and daily numbers are capped. Pileh Lagoon nearby is a channel of deep green water enclosed by cliffs on every side.

Two distinct reef systems are snorkelled, which is more than most trips on this route manage, and lunch is a Thai buffet on Phi Phi Don, the inhabited island.

The return leg takes in the Krabi four islands with sunset over the karst coastline from the water. The limestone holds colour long after the sun is down, so the light lasts past the point you expect it to finish.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers hotel pickup and drop-off in Ao Nang and Krabi Town, the premium speed catamaran with crew, an English-speaking guide, Thai buffet lunch and light refreshments.

Nine hours. National park fees are collected at the pier unless confirmed otherwise, so carry cash. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Speed catamaran, far steadier than a monohull in chop
Maya Bay under post-2022 rules: walk in, capped numbers
Pileh Lagoon, enclosed by cliffs on every side
Two separate reef systems snorkelled
Sunset over the karsts on the way home

fullDescription:
The four-island circuit run as a hostel trip, which changes the company more than the route.

The islands are the same ones every Krabi boat visits: Poda, Chicken Island with its rock formation, Tup and Mor linked by the Thale Waek sandbar at low tide. What is different is that this one departs from Nomads Krabi and Base Ao Nang Beach and fills with their guests, so the group skews young, solo and sociable rather than family-with-cooler-box.

Thale Waek, the Separated Sea, is the part worth timing. The sandbar surfaces as the tide drops and links three islands into one walkable strip, then vanishes as the water comes back. Whether you can walk it depends entirely on when you are there.

Snorkelling is over shallow coral just off Chicken Island, close enough to the beach that you do not need to be a confident swimmer to see it.

The price is genuinely all-in in a way that is rare on this coast: national park fees are included rather than collected at the pier, and lunch, water all day and a beer are covered. Nothing is collected at the ticket booth, so the price here is the price of the day.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers lunch, national park fees, water throughout the day, one beer, insurance, and pickup and drop-off at Nomads Krabi or Base Ao Nang Beach.

Six hours, minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Hostel departure, so a younger and more social group
Walk the Thale Waek sandbar at low tide
Snorkel shallow coral off Chicken Island
National park fees included, not charged at the pier
Lunch, water all day and a beer in the price
